newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany wants harsher sentences for sex crimes.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants harsher sentences for sex crimes.

text.p: The German cabinet on Tuesday approved a draft law which would make punishment for sex crimes harsher to try to protect children from sexual abuse.
Under the bill to be presented to the lower house of parliament this week, there will be longer jail sentences for a range of sex crimes against children.
The bill aims to end a discrepancy in the law which means that a bag snatcher can be jailed for up to 15 years, while a sex offender can only be imprisoned for a maximum of 10 years.
"The changes in the law are a vitally necessary step for the protection of our children from sexual violence," said Family Minister Claudia Nolte.
The bill would introduce a minimum sentence of one year for child sexual abuse and raise the maximum sentence to 15 years.
Sexual abuse will be defined as a crime and not just a misdemeanour, and convicted sex offenders will receive more therapy.
